title: Basic Adipocyte Culture Protocol
author: K.C. Kent Lloyd
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7bvhin6
materials: Day 1 Media Preparation: Place buffer in incubator to warm. Turn on shaking water bath to 37 degrees. Place 6 ml (pre-aliquoted and frozen) tubes of FBS (Omega FB-02), nystatin (N1638 Sigma), 3 ml penicillin/streptomycin (15140-122 GIBCO) (all in FC freezer) in incubator to thaw. Get 500 ml bottle of DMEM (11885-084 GIBCO) from walk-in cold room ( check glucose content—need low glucose (5mM)!! !). Place microfuge tube of insulin stock in hood to thaw (-80 freezer#1, top shelf, FC insulin box). Place microfuge tube of 100uCi/ml C14 glucose (New England Nuclear NEC-042) stock in hood to thaw (-20 freezer, FC C14 glucose stock). Turn on hood light in order to turn off uv. Make basic media by adding 6 ml each of FBS, nystatin, 3 ml penicillin/strep and 6 ml nonessential amino acids (11140-050 GIBCO in FC refrigerator) to 500 ml DMEM. Make medias (depending on the experimental reagents to be added, this can be the most difficult, intensive, and time-consuming part). Assume that 3ml media are needed per well (2ml added on Day 0, and .3 ml replaced at Day 1,2,3.). In order to make up .02 uCi/ml media for lipogenesis work, add .2 ul/ml media. Prepare insulin. • Dilute the 1mg/ml stock insulin (SIGMA I5523—original dilution 10mg in .01M HCl—150ul aliquots) 10Xs (.1 ml to 1.0 ml) • Sterilize with .2 um syringe filter. • Label it 160 nM insulin stock. • Dilute 160 nM insulin stock 100Xs (.1 ml to 10 mls). • Label it 1.6 nM insulin stock. • Mix well. • Dilute 1.6 nM insulin stock to 0.48 nM stock and label (1.5 ml to 5 mls). • Dilute 1.6 nM insulin stock to 0.16 nM stock and label (1ml to 10 mls). Add the appropriate amount of insulin to medias. 10 microliters of the insulin stock added to 1 ml of media = conc of stock label insulin media (i.e. 100 microliters of 1.6 nM insulin stock to 10 ml of media = 1.6 nM insulin media). Mix medias well, loosen lids, and store in incubator (6% CO2) until needed. Place extra DMEM in incubator until needed.
Pre-labeled pans are in the Plexiglas desiccators.
Keep a foil cover over weighed pans.

Glucose Oxidation Protocol All work areas and equipment used will be defined/labelled with tape “Caution-Radioactive Materials.” Personnel will wear lab coats, closed-toed shoes and disposable gloves. The 1000 uCi of C14 glucose is reconstituted in 1 ml sterile dd water and transferred to sterile 125 ml reagent jar. Use 4 more exact 1 ml pipeting of sterile dd water to clean C14 vial, transferring each to the reagent bottle. Add 95 ml sterile dd water to reagent bottle to dilute C14 to 10 uCi/ml. Aliquot into 200 sterile microfuge tubes, 500 ul each, and stored in labeled freezer box in the -20 freezer. The work bench of the sterile hood in room 3430 is lined with absorbent counter paper and the dry C14 waste container is moved to the vicinity of the hood. The C14 glucose is added to culture media at a concentration of 0.03 uCi/ml (3ul per ml) using disposable pipet tips in a disposable 50 ml falcon tube. Any unused portion of the C14 glucose glucose stock is marked T (for thawed) on top of tube and returned to the freezer box and the –20ºC freezer. All large volume pipeting of radioactive media is done using disposable pipets. All pipets, tips and empty tubes are disposed in the dry C14 radioactive waste immediately after use. All prepared media are labeled with radioactive label tape and stored in an incubator which is also labeled with radioactive tape. Cells isolated from rat adipose tissue are plated in 25 ml glass scintillation vials and 2 ml of the radioactive media (0.03 uCi/ml) is applied. The vials are capped using a rubber stopper which has been fitted with a polystyrene hanging well containing a 2 cm x 8 cm strip of Whatman #1 filter paper. Vials are gassed with 5% CO2 for 15 seconds using vent/delivery needles. Cells are maintained for 48 hr in a 37ºC incubator which is labeled as containing radioactive material. After 48 hr, 1000 ul of media is removed from each vial using a needle and 1 cc syringe. To minimize waste, the same needle and syringe is rinsed with plain/old DMEN and used for all samples. Used rinse media is placed in a labeled C14 waste bottle. Needles are discarded into a C14 radioactive-labeled sharps box and syringes are discarded into a dry C14-labeled radioactive waste bin. The 1000 ul media samples are placed in microfuge tubes and stored in a radioactive-labeled freezer box (also labeled as oxidation samples--FC XX). After media samples are removed, 200 ul of benzethonium hydroxide, a chemical which binds carbon dioxide, is applied by needle and syringe onto the filter paper in the hanging well through the rubber stopper (same needle is used for all samples). The needle is discarded into a C14 radioactive-labeled sharps box and the syringe is discarded into a dry C14 labeled radioactive waste bin. The C14 glucose oxidized by the cells to CO2 is absorbed onto the benzethonium hydroxide-soaked filter paper. Cells are lysed by the addition of 3 drops sulfuric acid delivered with needle/syringe through rubber stopper (same needle is used for all samples). All needles are placed in a radioactive-labeled sharp box and syringes are placed in the dry radioactive waste. After an overnight wait, the rubber stopper is removed from the vial and the hanging well is clipped with small wire cutters into a clean 25 ml scintillation vial containing scintillation fluid and the radioactivity is counted by a scintillation counter. One hundred ul aliquots of the unconditioned treatment media is also counted in 25 ml aqueous based scintillation fluid to determine total dpms added to vials. The rubber stopper is disposed in the dry radioactive waste. The wire cutters are washed three times with RBS, and the RBS is discarded into liquid C14 radioactive waste. Both the scintillation vials used for culture and used for counting are labeled as radioactive and stored in vial flats until they are collected by EH&S. All procedures (adding media, removing media samples, adding sulfuric acid, adding benzethinium hydroxide, removing stopper and well) are performed on absorbent counter paper, which is surveyed for contamination and placed in dry radioactive waste if contaminated. Paper that becomes contaminated with spilled radioactive media is cut out and disposed of into dry C14 radioactive waste. A count rate survey meter will be used to check work areas for contamination during and after each experiment. Paper that becomes contaminated with spilled radioactive media is cut out and disposed of into dry C14 radioactive waste. 24 hours later vials can be loaded onto scintillation counter. Make sure the first vial is a blank marked PJH C14 Rm3426. Sign the logbook. To start counter, hit ready 2xs, then 2 enter, 2 enter. Remove the vials the next day, and carefully label DPM data sheet with FC # and each count with vial label

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Supplies
steps.instruction: Prepare all necessary materials the day before the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Make phosphate-hepes buffer.

Autoclave Nalgene incubation jars (30 ml for mice, Fisher 02-925-1a), nytex filters (250 um PGC 34-1800-03; 450 um for subcutaneous depot PGC 34-1800-09), long needles (+6, Fisher 14-825-16H), 1 ml and 0.2 ml pipet tips, surgical equipment (3-5 small scissors, 3 large scissors, 3 forceps), and reagent jars (500 ml, 250 ml, and 100 ml).
Cut 6-inch PE tubing (Clay Adams PE-205) for aspirating needles and sterilize under UV.
Clean the hood and turn on UV light.

steps.title: Set Up Animal Processing Station
steps.instruction: Prepare the workspace and materials for animal sacrifice and sample collection.

substeps.instruction: Cut and label lab coverings for each carcass with animal # (absorbent side up).
Label two sterile 60 mm culture dishes per animal; place one dry by the microbalance and add buffer to the other.
Place surgical equipment in a beaker with 70% EtOH.
Fill a labeled 15 ml conical tube with buffer.
Label an EDTA purple top vacutainer with ID, place a small plastic funnel in the tube, and set the lid aside.
Prepare ice for blood samples and place the FC notebook by the microbalance.

steps.title: Prepare Collagenase Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the collagenase solution (Worthington 4197) based on the expected fat weight.

substeps.instruction: Calculate concentration: 0.625 mg/ml (2 ml/gram of fat, assuming 1 gram of fat per mouse).
Transfer 5 mg dry collagenase to a 50 ml conical tube and add 8 ml buffer (Standard 6-10 mouse recipe: 12.5 mg collagenase per 20 ml buffer).
Mix well, sterilize with steriflip, and store in the incubator until needed.

steps.title: Animal Sacrifice and Blood Collection
steps.instruction: Euthanize the animal and collect blood.

substeps.instruction: Place animal in kill jar with isoflurane.
Once unconscious, weigh and record the animal.
Decapitate and collect truncal blood in the funnel/EDTA tube.
Seal the blood tube, invert, and store on ice.

steps.title: Isolate and Weigh Fat Pads
steps.instruction: Extract the fat pads and record their weight under sterile conditions.

substeps.instruction: Remove epididymal and/or mesenteric fat pads using buffer-rinsed surgical equipment.
Place fat pads in a labeled culture dish with buffer.
Tare the dry labeled culture dish on the microbalance.
Transfer the fat pad to the dish using buffer-rinsed forceps, weigh, and record.
If the fat pad exceeds 4-4.5 grams, remove excess fat using buffer-rinsed scissors and record the final suspension weight.

steps.title: Digest Fat Pads
steps.instruction: Mince the fat and incubate with collagenase to release adipocytes.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 ml of collagenase per gram of fat to labeled suspension jars.
Transfer the fat pad to the lid of the culture dish and mince for 1-2 minutes.
Transfer minced fat to the incubation jar with collagenase using a cell scraper.
Parafilm the lid, record the start time, and place in a 37°C shaking water bath (motor setting 6) for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Filter and Wash Adipocytes
steps.instruction: Filter the digested suspension and wash the cells to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 15 ml conical tubes with 250 um filters forced into place with a 10 ml pipette.
After 30 minutes of incubation, remove the jar, add 10 ml buffer, and pipette up and down 4 times to mix.
Transfer the suspension to the filter and allow it to drain; gently scrape the filter into the tube if necessary.
Add buffer up to 14 ml and centrifuge at 900 rpm for 6 minutes.
Remove the buffer and stromal vascular layer from beneath the cell layer using a 20 ml syringe with a 6-inch 18 gauge needle and PE tube cover; discard in waste beaker.
Add 10-14 ml fresh buffer and centrifuge at 900 rpm for 6 minutes.
Remove buffer and replace with 8-10 ml warm basic media; centrifuge at 900 rpm for 6 minutes.
Remove media and add fresh buffer/media up to 14 ml; incubate for at least 30 minutes (up to 3 hours).

steps.title: Prepare Collagen Plating Matrix
steps.instruction: Prepare the collagen solution for plating.

substeps.instruction: Calculate collagen (Cohesion Technologies 00701) needed: 0.3 ml/well plus 3-5 ml extra; transfer to a sterile container.
Add 1 ml 10X DMEM stock (GIBCO 41500-034) per 10 ml collagen.
Adjust pH to 7 (red color) using 10M NaOH (starting at 1 ul/ml) and 1M NaOH (adding 1-5 ul at a time).
Set up pipettes: 1 ml pipette for 0.3 ml (wells), 200 ul pipette for 0.15 ml (vials) and 0.05 ml (media). Use 50 ml conical tubes to hold pipettes to maintain sterility.

steps.title: Plate Adipocytes
steps.instruction: Seed the isolated adipocytes onto the collagen matrix in 6-well plates.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the cell suspension: remove media from under the cell pack, centrifuge for 2 minutes at 500 rpm, and remove the extracellular lipid from the top and media from the bottom.
Pipette 0.3 ml collagen into the middle of each well.
Add 0.05 ml basic media to the top of the collagen mound in each well (including a 'no cell' control well).
Using a wide-bevel tip (ART 200G/Fisher 21-236-1A), draw 50-200 ul of fat suspension from the center of the cell pack (50 ul for young lean mice <24g; 75-100 ul for older/fatter animals).
Pipette the suspension directly onto the collagen/media droplet in all wells except the 'no cell' well.
Replace the lid, label the plate, and gently spread the collagen across the bottom of the wells.
Place the plate in the incubator immediately to set.
After at least 40 minutes, carefully add 2 ml of appropriate media to each well (including 'no cell' wells) and return to the incubator.

steps.title: Collect Daily Media Samples
steps.instruction: Sample media from the cultures over four days.

substeps.instruction: Day 1: Sample from each well into labeled microfuge tubes; replace with 0.3 ml appropriate media. Freeze samples.
Day 2: Sample 0.3 ml from each well; replace with 0.3 ml appropriate media. Freeze samples.
Day 3: Sample 0.3 ml from each well; replace with 0.3 ml appropriate media. Freeze samples.
Day 4: Sample 1 ml from each well into labeled microfuge tubes. Freeze samples.

steps.title: Harvest Intracellular Lipids
steps.instruction: Extract lipids from the cells on Day 4.

substeps.instruction: Remove media and as much extracellular lipid as possible using a vacuum flask/Pasteur pipet (if the cell layer is firm).
If the layer is not firm, use 250 um mesh circles to protect cells, remove media/lipid with a pipette, add 1-2 ml warm basic media, swirl, let lipid rise, and then aspirate.
Rinse with 1 ml warm basic media and aspirate again.
Wipe remaining lipid from the well edges with a cotton swab on a stick.
Add 4 ml methanol to each well, Parafilm, cover with a lid, and refrigerate until transfer to Folch tubes.

steps.title: Determine Total Intracellular Lipid
steps.instruction: Perform the Folch method to quantify lipids under a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: 24 hours after adding chloroform, add dH2O to within 0.5 inches of the Folch tube top, reseal, and invert 2-3 times.
Once the chloroform layer is clear, aspirate the top water/methanol layer, retaining at least 8 ml of chloroform.
Weigh pre-labeled pans to the 4th decimal place and place on a foil-lined tray.
Pipette 1 ml of chloroform into labeled scintillation vials and allow to evaporate overnight under the hood.
Pipette 5 ml of chloroform from each tube into the corresponding weighed pan and allow to evaporate overnight under the hood.
Add 15 ml Ecolume scintillation fluid to the vials; prepare a separate vial with 100 ul of corresponding media and 15 ml Ecolume fluid.
Load vials onto the scintillation counter (starting with blank PJH C14 Rm3426) and record DPM data the next day.
Weigh the evaporated pans (touching only outside rims), subtract the initial pan weight, and multiply by 2 (for 5 ml pipette) to determine total intracellular lipid.
